# ci-manager-github

**Realize GitHub-side resources from one token, and record what it made.**

A forge-ci `manager` engine.

## Why it exists

Bootstrap is a reconcile like any other. The engine that uses GitHub
declares what must exist there - workflow files, Actions secrets, enablement -
and this manager makes it so from one PAT, so a new pipeline instance needs
nothing clicked and nothing scripted.

## Tools

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `reconcile` | Realize every declared GitHub resource and return who owns it. |

## By hand

```sh
echo '{"manager":"github","resources":[{"kind":"actions-secret","name":"o/r/FORGE_CI_GITHUB_TOKEN","spec":{"repo":"o/r","secret":"FORGE_CI_GITHUB_TOKEN"}}]}' \
  | ci-manager-github reconcile
```

## In a pipeline

```yaml
engines:
  - alias: my-manager
    type: manager
    engine: "forge://github.com/alexandremahdhaoui/forge-ci/cmd/ci-manager-github@v0.1.0"
    manager: local
    spec:
      statePath: <string>
      apiBaseURL: <string>
      tokenEnv: <string>
```

## Worth knowing

It knows three kinds. `file-content` converges a file on the local
checkout to the declared content - drift included, unlike the local manager's
`file`, which keeps what exists. `actions-secret` seals the value of the named
environment variable (default GITHUB_TOKEN) against the repo key and puts it -
the secrets API is write-only, so the put is the convergence, and existence is
the only state it can read back. `workflow-enabled` enables a workflow by file
name; a workflow not yet on the remote reports pending instead of failing, and
the reconcile after the first push completes it.

A reconcile that changed anything answers `changed: true`, and it makes the
change durable before it answers: the converged files are committed and pushed
on the branch each checkout is on, staging only the paths that changed. A
checkout with no origin or a detached HEAD is committed and not pushed, and
says so. A caller stops the run on `changed`, because the tree it was about to
measure is the tree this reconcile just rewrote.

A bootstrap converges and never commits. It is run by an operator who is about
to look at what it wrote, and it runs no stages, so there is nothing to stop.

There is no delete path: a resource dropped from a spec stays as it is,
exactly like the local manager. It refuses a resource recorded as owned by a
different manager.

The token is read from the environment at realize time and never written to
state, actions or logs.
